sentences.en: I'm Gemma Spegg, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through the biggest changes, moments, and transitions of our 20s,
sentences.zh: 我是杰玛·斯佩格，欢迎回到《二十岁心理学》，在这里，我们一起探讨二十岁时面临的重大改变、时刻与转折点，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理的意义。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本播客。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining me.
sentences.zh: 感谢大家的收听。

sentences.en: Wherever you are in the world, it is very great to have you here.
sentences.zh: 无论你身处世界的哪一个角落，很高兴能在这里与你相聚。

sentences.en: Today, I have another bonus episode for you.
sentences.zh: 今天，我为大家准备了另一期加更节目。

sentences.en: If you are new to this corner of the podcast, in our bonus episodes, we basically fact-check and myth-bust psychology concepts
sentences.zh: 如果你是刚来到这个播客的角落，在我们的加更节目中，我们基本上会核实事实并粉碎那些心理学概念的谣言，

sentences.en: that you may have heard kind of swirling around the internet a little bit, and we basically provide you with the real research, the real history,
sentences.zh: 这些概念你可能在互联网上略有耳闻，我们基本上会为你提供它们背后的真实研究、真实历史，

sentences.en: and the real science behind what they mean.
sentences.zh: 以及它们所代表的真实科学。

sentences.en: We've done personality tests.
sentences.zh: 我们聊过人格测试。

sentences.en: We've done Stockholm Syndrome,
sentences.zh: 我们聊过斯德哥尔摩综合征，

sentences.en: narcissism,
sentences.zh: 自恋，

sentences.en: Maslow's hierarchy of needs, so many things, but today we are turning our sights and our attention to shadow work.
sentences.zh: 马斯洛的需求层次理论，还有好多好多，但今天，我们将目光和注意力转向阴影工作（Shadow Work）。

sentences.en: Shadow work is a practice that is focused on what we call the shadow self, or just the shadow, and how this part of us influences our behavior unconsciously.
sentences.zh: 阴影工作是一种专注于我们所谓的“阴影自我”（或简称“阴影”），以及这一部分如何无意识地影响我们行为的实践。

sentences.en: If you have ever done any kind of psychotherapy or psychoanalysis, you're probably very familiar with this concept or idea, but it's become exceedingly popular in recent years.
sentences.zh: 如果你曾经做过任何形式的心理治疗或精神分析，你可能对这个概念或想法非常熟悉，但在近年来，它变得异常流行。

sentences.en: As people have kind of been searching for deeper ways of meeting and knowing themselves.
sentences.zh: 因为人们一直在寻找更深层次的方式来认识和了解自己。

sentences.en: This approach is definitely an interesting one because it kind of promises a good deal of epiphanies, and it really promises the possibility
sentences.zh: 这种方法绝对很有意思，因为它似乎承诺了大量的顿悟，并且切实承诺了

sentences.en: of suddenly uncovering some really deep truths about why you are the way you are, and, you know, who you are, and, you know, for a lot of us,
sentences.zh: 突然揭开一些关于你为什么会成为现在的你、你是谁的深层真相的可能性，而且，你知道的，对我们中的许多人来说，

sentences.en: that's comforting that there's this thing out there that can suddenly reveal why we self-sabotage, why we act in the way that we do.
sentences.zh: 有一种慰藉，那就是有这样一种东西，能够突然揭示为什么我们会自我破坏，为什么我们会做出那样的行为。

sentences.en: But I think you also should be prepared to find out some stuff you might not want to know about who you are.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得你也应该做好准备，去发现一些关于你是谁的、你可能并不想知道的事情。

sentences.en: So let's break down just what shadow work really entails from the most basic principles to some of the more advanced practices.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们从最基础的原则到一些更高级的实践，来剖析一下阴影工作究竟包含什么。

sentences.en: So I think the first thing you should know is what the shadow actually is.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得你需要了解的第一件事就是，阴影究竟是什么。

sentences.en: I gave a brief explanation, but the shadow essentially represents the aspects of yourself that you don't like and that you don't want to be associated with
sentences.zh: 我做了一个简短的解释，但本质上，阴影代表了你身上那些你不喜欢、不希望与之产生联系，

sentences.en: and therefore find it very difficult to acknowledge and recognize.
sentences.zh: 因此觉得很难去承认和认知的那些方面。

sentences.en: The first thing you should know about shadow work is who created it.
sentences.zh: 关于阴影工作，你首先应该了解的是是谁创造了它。

sentences.en: That's a great place to start.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的切入点。

sentences.en: The idea came from Carl Jung, who we have been mentioning a lot recently.
sentences.zh: 这个概念来自卡尔·荣格，我们最近经常提到他。

sentences.en: So if you're a frequent listener,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是老听众，

sentences.en: I'm sorry, but also I don't know how much to revisit for the basics.
sentences.zh: 我很抱歉，但同时我也在纠结对于基础知识到底该复习多少。

sentences.en: But simply,
sentences.zh: 但简而言之，

sentences.en: Carl Jung was a Swiss psychiatriSt.
sentences.zh: 卡尔·荣格是一位瑞士精神病学家。

sentences.en: He was a psychoanalyst and he developed analytical psychology, which is the school of psychological thought, which is very much focused on the unconscious mind
sentences.zh: 他是一名精神分析学家，并创立了分析心理学，这是心理学思想的一个流派，非常专注于无意识心理，

sentences.en: and the realization of our true self through a lifelong process that he called individuation.
sentences.zh: 以及通过他称之为“个性化”（individuation）的终生过程来实现我们真正的自我。

sentences.en: Now, Jung's approach was very deep.
sentences.zh: 荣格的方法非常深奥。

sentences.en: It was very inward focused.
sentences.zh: 它高度聚焦于内心。

sentences.en: It was very much concerned with symbols and dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 它非常关注象征和梦境。

sentences.en: And he had a lot of similarities to Freud.
sentences.zh: 而且他与弗洛伊德有很多相似之处。

sentences.en: I say similarities.
sentences.zh: 我说的是相似之处。

sentences.en: He actually originally trained under Sigmund Freud, the grandfather of modern psychology.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他最初师从西格蒙德·弗洛伊德，现代心理学之祖。

sentences.en: And you'll know that if you listen to our Freud episode.
sentences.zh: 如果你听过我们的弗洛伊德单集，你就会知道这一点。

sentences.en: And at the time, he was kind of considered his successor.
sentences.zh: 在当时，他被认为是弗洛伊德的继任者。

sentences.en: You know, the baton was going to be passed from Jung.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，接力棒将从荣格手中……

sentences.en: Oh, sorry, from Freud to Jung.
sentences.zh: 哦，抱歉，是从弗洛伊德传给荣格。

sentences.en: But they eventually parted ways.
sentences.zh: 但他们最终分道扬镳了。

sentences.en: Professionally and personally, they had these series of major disagreements.
sentences.zh: 在职业和个人层面上，他们发生了一系列重大分歧。

sentences.en: They had beef, as we would say in the modern day.
sentences.zh: 用现代的话说，他们结下了梁子（beef）。

sentences.en: Beef is probably an understatement.
sentences.zh: 用“结下梁子”来形容可能都有点保守了。

sentences.en: The way they expressed this, like these disagreements, was that they would write these like research papers and these articles in academic magazines and journals
sentences.zh: 他们表达这些分歧的方式是，在学术杂志和期刊上写一篇又一篇的研究论文和文章，

sentences.en: back and forth and back and forth, obviously about the other one, about the other person.
sentences.zh: 你来我往，显然全都是针对对方的。

sentences.en: And the reason for this disagreement was that Freud was also focused on the unconscious mind, but he was very much focused on sexual and aggressive impulses.
sentences.zh: 产生这种分歧的原因在于，弗洛伊德同样专注于无意识心灵，但他非常专注于性和攻击性冲动。

sentences.en: And he saw the unconscious largely as this place where there was repressed material from early childhood that we had to dig at.
sentences.zh: 他主要将无意识视为这样一个地方：里面存有来自幼儿期、需要我们去发掘的压抑材料。

sentences.en: And Jung kind of agreed in some ways.
sentences.zh: 荣格在某些方面表示赞同。

sentences.en: He said the unconscious mind was important.
sentences.zh: 他认为无意识心灵非常重要。

sentences.en: There were definitely things there that we couldn't access.
sentences.zh: 里面确实存在我们无法触及的东西。

sentences.en: But he thought that the idea that a lot of those impulses were sexual or aggressive was too narrow.
sentences.zh: 但他认为，许多冲动源于性和攻击性的这种观点过于狭隘了。

sentences.en: You know, he really wanted to expand this idea and he wanted to talk about symbols and religion and myths and dreams and what he called the collective unconscious.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他真的很想拓展这个概念，他想谈论象征、宗教、神话、梦境，以及他所称的集体无意识。

sentences.en: The collective unconscious was this idea that beyond our own individual unconscious, there is a deeper level, a deeper layer of shared psychological patterns
sentences.zh: 集体无意识是指这样一种观点：在我们的个人无意识之外，还有一个更深层次、更深层的共享心理模式层，

sentences.en: that all humans inherit.
sentences.zh: 这是所有人类共同继承的。

sentences.en: And these patterns show up across cultures, across time, across history, and he labeled them as the archetypes.
sentences.zh: 这些模式跨越文化、跨越时间、跨越历史反复出现，他将其命名为原型（archetypes）。

sentences.en: So the archetypes, this is the first critical thing you need to understand if you want to get into shadow work, are these instinctual patterns that are common
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想深入了解阴影工作，你需要理解的第一个关键事物就是原型，它们是存在于

sentences.en: amongst every single culture, every single human across history.
sentences.zh: 历史上每一个文化、每一个人类之中的本能模式。

sentences.en: He basically believed that we all have this built-in psychological software or psychological patterns that shape the human mind and shape the human experience.
sentences.zh: 他基本上相信，我们都内置了这种心理软件或心理模式，塑造了人类的心智和人类的体验。

sentences.en: For example, every single human has the self which brings all of our personality together.
sentences.zh: 例如，每个人都有“自我”（self），它将我们的人格融为一体。

sentences.en: Every single human has a shadow which we're talking about today.
sentences.zh: 每个人都有一个“阴影”，也就是我们今天正在讨论的内容。

sentences.en: They have a persona which is what they kind of use to cover up the parts of themselves that they don't like.
sentences.zh: 他们有一个“面具”（persona），也就是他们用来掩盖自己不喜欢的那部分自我的东西。

sentences.en: And then there's something called the anima and the animus which we're going to reserve for a whole separate episode.
sentences.zh: 然后还有一种叫做“阿尼玛”和“阿尼姆斯”的东西，我们将留到单独的一整期节目中再讲。

sentences.en: Now, those are the four components of like the unconscious mind or basically not the unconscious mind but our architecture as humans, as feeling humans.
sentences.zh: 现在，这些是无意识心灵的四个组成部分，或者说基本上不是无意识心灵，而是我们作为人类、作为有感知力的人类的架构。

sentences.en: And then there are these additional aspects which are called the archetypes and this is how each of these different parts is channeled.
sentences.zh: 此外，还有一些被称为原型的附加方面，这就是这些不同部分的引导方式。

sentences.en: So the archetypes are the templates or patterns that shape how we experience certain roles or themes in our lives.
sentences.zh: 因此，原型是塑造我们如何体验生活中某些角色或主题的模板或模式。

sentences.en: So the common ones that you might hear people talk about include the caregiver, the hero, the jester, the lover, the ruler, the rebel.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会听到人们谈论的常见角色包括照顾者、英雄、小丑、情人、统治者、叛逆者。

sentences.en: This is actually where personality tests like Maya Briggs come from.
sentences.zh: 迈尔斯-布里格斯（MBTI）这样的人格测试实际上就源于此。

sentences.en: If you've ever done a personality test and it's given you a four-letter acronym that is meant to describe everything about who you are know that this came from Jung and his work
sentences.zh: 如果你曾经做过人格测试，它给出了一个旨在描述你一切特征的四字母缩写，要知道这源于荣格以及他

sentences.en: with archetypes and the shadow.
sentences.zh: 对原型和阴影的研究。

sentences.en: So you've encountered the theory before but each of these archetypes and I gave you a couple you know the hero, the jester, etc.
sentences.zh: 所以你以前接触过这个理论，但每一个原型——我举了几个例子，你知道的，英雄、小丑等——

sentences.en: They each seek something different and they have a different role in society and for us personally.
sentences.zh: 它们各自追求不同的东西，并在社会以及我们个人身上扮演着不同的角色。

sentences.en: Their role is either to provide structure, to connect to others, to leave a mark or to provide wisdom.
sentences.zh: 它们的作用要么是提供结构，要么是连接他人，要么是留下印记，要么是提供智慧。

sentences.en: Within that each archetype then seeks something and embodies this role as a way to obtain the thing it seeks.
sentences.zh: 在此基础之上，每个原型都有所追求，并将其角色具体化，以此作为获得所求之物的一种方式。

sentences.en: So for example the ruler archetype
sentences.zh: 例如，统治者原型

sentences.en: creates order in society and what they really deep down want as a ruler is control.
sentences.zh: 在社会中建立秩序，作为一个统治者，他们内心深处真正想要的是控制。

sentences.en: They really need control to feel psychologically safe.
sentences.zh: 他们确实需要控制来获得心理上的安全感。

sentences.en: The outlaw is another archetype and they really need liberation.
sentences.zh: 叛逆者是另一个原型，他们真正需要的是解放。

sentences.en: So they seek liberation through everything that they do.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们在自己所做的每一件事中都在寻求解放。

sentences.en: The everyman seeks belonging, the artist seeks innovation.
sentences.zh: 凡人寻求归属感，艺术家寻求创新。

sentences.en: we typically lean towards one and we see these archetypes in nearly every society and they play out again and again and again.
sentences.zh: 我们通常倾向于其中一种，我们在几乎每个社会中都能看到这些原型，它们一遍又一遍地上演。

sentences.en: However we can shift between them.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们可以在它们之间切换。

sentences.en: We lean towards one but we shift between them.
sentences.zh: 我们虽然倾向于其中一个，但我们会在它们之间切换。

sentences.en: So if you have what
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你拥有荣格所谓的

sentences.en: Jung would call like a healthy mature personality you could be and you could embody the ruler when you were leading a project but you could also embody the caregiver when you were
sentences.zh: 健康成熟的人格，你可以在领导项目时成为并体现统治者，但当你在

sentences.en: comforting a friend.
sentences.zh: 安慰朋友时，你也可以体现照顾者。

sentences.en: you could embody the explorer when you were traveling.
sentences.zh: 当你旅行时，你可以体现探险家。

sentences.en: Now each of these archetypes has kind of a light expression which is like the general way that they present but there is also a shadow expression that develops when the role
sentences.zh: 现在，这些原型中的每一个都有着某种“光明表达”，也就是它们呈现的通常方式，但也有“阴影表达”，这会在过度认同某个角色、

sentences.en: becomes over identified with and when we become obsessed with what our archetype seeks and it's then the role of the persona to kind of cover up how it goes about seeking them
sentences.zh: 当我们痴迷于我们的原型所追求的东西时发展出来，这时面具（persona）的作用就是掩盖它是如何通过

sentences.en: in these kind of darker parts of ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们自身这些更黑暗的部分来追求这些东西的。

sentences.en: So the caregiver for example in its lighter form is about compassion and support and generosity and looking after others but when it becomes ego driven it can turn into overgiving,
sentences.zh: 例如，照顾者在其较光明的一面关乎同情心、支持、慷慨以及照顾他人，但当它变得由自我（ego）驱动时，就会变成过度付出、

sentences.en: people pleasing,
sentences.zh: 讨好他人、

sentences.en: codependency, needing to be needed in order to feel worthy.
sentences.zh: 共依存，为了感到有价值而需要被需要。

sentences.en: The shadow side then takes that a step further and can involve resentment,
sentences.zh: 阴暗面则会将其推进一步，可能涉及怨恨、

sentences.en: using care as a way to gain approval or power, needing control through caring for others and that shadow side is the stuff that we don't want to acknowledge when we speak about
sentences.zh: 利用关怀作为获得认可或权力的手段、通过照顾他人来寻求控制，而这种阴暗面正是我们在谈论自己是一个富有同情心的人时

sentences.en: ourselves as a caring person.
sentences.zh: 不想承认的东西。

sentences.en: We don't want to acknowledge and we rarely will acknowledge how that behavior and that desire can sometimes become ugly.
sentences.zh: 我们不想承认，也极少会承认这种行为和欲望有时会变得多么丑陋。

sentences.en: I'll give you another example.
sentences.zh: 我再举个例子。

sentences.en: The hero archetype is another one that you might hear about a lot.
sentences.zh: 英雄原型是你可能会经常听到的另一个原型。

sentences.en: In its outward facing form, it's about courage, it's about growth and facing challenges but when this becomes ego driven, it can turn into needing to prove ourselves, constantly
sentences.zh: 在其外显的形式中，它关乎勇气、成长和直面挑战，但当它被自我驱动时，就会变成需要证明自己、不断

sentences.en: pushing, seeing everything as a battle that we have to win and the shadow side of that shows up as arrogance, hyper competitiveness, maybe hurting others or an inability to ask
sentences.zh: 逼迫自己、把每件事都视为必须赢的战斗，而它的阴暗面则表现为傲慢、过度竞争、或许会伤害他人或是无法开口

sentences.en: for help.
sentences.zh: 寻求帮助。

sentences.en: The final one I should talk about,
sentences.zh: 我要谈的最后一个，

sentences.en: I'm going to give one more example, I feel like examples are the best way to make this known, is the jester.
sentences.zh: 我再举一个例子，我觉得举例是让人理解这点的最好方式，那就是小丑。

sentences.en: Now the jester brings humor and lightness and connection but when it becomes a rigidly fixed identity, it can turn into deflecting everything with jokes, avoiding
